Wir sind ein Team von Techniker:innen und Ingenieur:innen, das aus hervorragenden Teamplayern besteht und von erfahrenen Führungskräften geleitet wird. Wir arbeiten gemeinsam daran, die Geräte in unserem gesamten globalen Netzwerk von Fulfillment-Centern zu warten, zu reparieren und ihre Fehler zu beheben. Einige unserer Mitarbeiter:innen sind Führungskräfte, die das Team bei der Arbeit an spannender, innovativer Technologie beaufsichtigen – die es teilweise nur bei Amazon gibt. Design, implement, and maintain automated test suites for in‑vehicle connectivity software and supporting tools, with a focus on regression stability and coverage. Develop system‑level and integration test cases that exercise edge cases, failure modes, roaming/hand‑off scenarios, and interoperability across ECUs, mobile devices, and backend services. Analyze requirements, architecture, and design documents to identify test gaps and proactively influence design for testability. Build and extend test frameworks, harnesses, and utilities (e.g., Python‑based automation, log parsing, simulators, stubs/mocks) to increase repeatability and execution speed. Perform hands‑on debug and triage of complex issues across Bluetooth/Digital Key, telematics control units, and network connectivity (WLAN, VLAN) layers; capture traces and logs and partner with development to root‑cause defects. Work with systems, cybersecurity, and performance teams to ensure connectivity software meets reliability, robustness, and security expectations. Contribute to continuous integration pipelines by integrating automated tests, stabilizing nightly/continuous runs, and reporting clear quality signals. Mentor more junior engineers in test design, automation best practices, and debugging techniques; help raise the overall bar for connectivity software verification. Provide clear, data‑driven quality status and risk assessments to stakeholders and leadership. Strong experience testing embedded or real‑time systems, ideally in automotive, mobile, telecom, or networking domains. Solid programming/scripting skills for test automation (e.g., Python; familiarity with C/C++ and/or Java is a plus). Practical knowledge of connectivity technologies such as: Digital Key / phone‑as‑a‑key solutions. Bluetooth/Bluetooth Low Energy (pairing, profiles, audio/data use cases). Network connectivity fundamentals (WLAN, VLAN, TCP/UDP, routing, DNS, security protocols). Experience designing and executing system‑level, integration, and regression tests, including negative, stress, and long‑run scenarios. Familiarity with test management and defect tracking tools, and with CI environments (e.g., Jenkins, Git‑based workflows). Strong debugging skills using logs, traces, and protocol analyzers (e.g., Bluetooth sniffers, network analyzers, CAN tools). Proven ability to work cross‑functionally in a fast‑paced engineering environment, communicate clearly, and drive issues to closure. Strong ownership mindset, attention to detail, and a passion for delivering high‑quality, customer‑facing features. What Will Give You a Competitive Edge (Preferred Skills) Experience testing in‑vehicle infotainment or automotive connectivity systems (Bluetooth, Wi‑Fi, Digital Key/BLE, telematics) across multiple ECU configurations. Experience with in‑vehicle networks and automotive protocols (e.g., CAN, LIN, SOME/IP, UDS, Ethernet in‑vehicle networking). Background in connectivity or infotainment domains within automotive, including prior work on telematics or similar connected‑services platforms. Hands‑on experience with Digital Key ecosystems (e.g., Bluetooth LE, UWB, NFC, secure storage, mobile app integration). Experience with: Automated test frameworks and CI/CD (e.g., Jenkins, GitHub Actions, or similar), Robot Framework or comparable automation stacks for bench and HIL testing. Prior mentoring or technical leadership experience within a verification or QA team. Background in correlating customer feedback (e.g., JD Power, Compass, call‑center tickets) with technical issues and feeding those learnings into test design and KPIs. Strong data analysis skills (e.g., dashboards, metrics) to derive insights from large volumes of test results and logs and to improve test efficiency and effectiveness. jobs.description:
SpaceXAI’s mission is to create AI systems that can accurately understand the universe and aid humanity in its pursuit of knowledge.
Our team is small, highly motivated, and focused on engineering excellence. This organization is for individuals who appreciate challenging themselves and thrive on curiosity.
We operate with a flat organizational structure. All employees are expected to be hands-on and to contribute directly to the company’s mission. Leadership is given to those who show initiative and consistently deliver excellence. Work ethic and strong prioritization skills are important.
All employees are expected to have strong communication skills. They should be able to concisely and accurately share knowledge with their teammates.
ABOUT THE ROLE:
Join the High Power Engineering team supporting SpaceXAI to design, build, operate, and maintain electrical infrastructure for AI training campuses. As a Lead Engineer for Battery Storage, you will work with a small on-site team to scale high-capacity power systems on a schedule set by compute demand. The position is based in Memphis, TN, with potential travel to other sites.
RESPONSIBILITIES:
Own the storage fleet as a power plant, not as an accessory: architecture, sizing, controls, safety case, and grid-forming behavior that lets the campus ride through compute step loads and generation contingencies.
Own BESS architecture: pack-to-MV-transformer grouping, string composition, medium-voltage collection topology, string-level protection, and physical block layout including spacing per NFPA 855.
Own sizing; translate compute duty cycles — step loads, training-job ramps, actual-versus-nameplate utilization — into power and energy requirements.
Own inverter control strategy: grid-forming versus grid-following, droop and virtual inertia, fault-current contribution, ride-through, and coordination with generation governors and excitation.
Own the plant controller and EMS functional specification: dispatch, state-of-charge management, peak shaving, spinning-reserve emulation, islanding, and black-start participation.
Own the fire and life-safety case: UL 9540 and 9540A basis, thermal runaway propagation, deflagration venting, water supply, emergency response plan, and AHJ engagement.
Own the OEM relationship: technical requirements, factory testing, performance guarantees, and degradation and augmentation planning.
Direct Design, Commissioning, Ops/Build, Network, Civil, and Program Manager seats on Battery Storage as those seats fill.
BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:
Bachelor's degree in electrical engineering, computer engineering, physics, or another engineering discipline.
8+ years in power systems engineering.
4+ years directly on utility-scale or large commercial and industrial battery energy storage.
PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCES:
Experience sizing storage against a real duty cycle rather than a rule of thumb.
Working knowledge of NFPA 855, UL 9540 and 9540A, IEEE 1547, and IEEE 2800.
Utility-scale BESS fleet experience at large pack counts.
Deep understanding of grid-forming inverter control and its interaction with synchronous machines.
PSCAD or other EMT modeling of inverter-based resources.
Professional Engineering license or intention to actively seek a PE license.
Experience building and leading an engineering team from the first hire.
ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:
Perform hands-on work in all environments (heat, cold, rain), in tight quarters or at heights.
Work extended hours and weekends as needed to support construction, energization, and operations.
Remain focused in hazardous environments while wearing appropriate PPE.
Lift up to 25 lbs. unassisted.
Provide 24/7 on-call support for emergencies.
Willing to work on-site in Memphis, TN. This is not a remote or hybrid role.
Travel up to 25% for factory witness testing, vendor and OEM engagement, and supporting other sites.
Valid driver's license.

jobs.description: Build a Career That Builds Your Future — with PulteGroup! Welcome to PulteGroup where we believe in building more than just homes—we believe in building inspired employees, meaningful careers, and a legacy of excellence. If you're looking for work that moves you, a team that values your ideas, and a company that brings you pride, you’ve come to the right place. As one of the nation’s largest and most respected homebuilders, PulteGroup offers opportunities to grow within a Fortune 500 company that’s consistently recognized as a Fortune 100 Best Company to Work For and a certified Great Place to Work. We’re driven by the bold purpose of Building Incredible Places for People to Live Their Dreams. For over 70 years, we’ve been building more than homes—we’ve been building trust, innovation, and a culture where every team member is empowered to thrive. Join a company that champions inclusion, celebrates diversity, and supports your personal and professional journey. Headquartered in vibrant Atlanta, Georgia, and operating in over 45 markets nationwide, we’re proud to build homes through our trusted family of brands—including Innovative Construction Group, Centex, Pulte Homes, Del Webb, DiVosta Homes, American West, and John Wieland Homes and Neighborhoods, Pulte Mortgage, PGP Title, Pulte Insurance Agency —all united under the PulteGroup name. Apply now and discover a career where your contributions are valued, your growth is supported, and your work makes a lasting impact The Senior Engineer will lead and provide advanced-level technical support for highly complex issues, as well as engineering and technology integration services for intricate systems and infrastructure. Spearhead team initiatives and participate in multiple IT project implementations simultaneously. With a deep understanding of advanced concepts, practices, and procedures, serves as a subject matter expert, considering both the current and future business environment in the design and upgrade of systems. Mentor and coach junior team members, fostering their professional growth and ensuring they adhere to best practices and standards. Primary Job Responsibilities Lead team initiatives and provide guidance to engineers. Act as a mentor to less experienced team members, providing technical guidance and support. Additionally, take on a leadership role in cross-functional teams and provide strategic direction for complex projects. Lead medium to large-scale IT projects, ensuring they are completed on time and within budget. Develop project plans, coordinate resources, and manage project timelines. Additionally, oversee multiple projects simultaneously and ensure alignment with organizational goals. Participate in strategic planning for IT infrastructure, including capacity planning and technology roadmaps. Evaluate and recommend new technologies to improve infrastructure performance and efficiency. Additionally, contribute to the development of long-term IT strategies and initiatives. Design and implement enterprise-class datacenter infrastructure. Plan and deploy virtualization solutions using private, public, and hybrid cloud technologies. Additionally, lead the design and implementation of complex, large-scale infrastructure projects. Plan and implement proactive management and monitoring solutions using enterprise-class tools. Ensure the reliability, performance, and availability of critical systems through advanced monitoring techniques. Additionally, develop and implement advanced monitoring and management strategies. Provide third-level technical support for complex infrastructure issues. Serve as an escalation point for resolving high-impact infrastructure challenges. Additionally, develop and implement advanced troubleshooting procedures and best practices. Helps implement optimal cloud resources for executing workloads and optimizing cloud spend. Participates in projects to establish and evolve DevOps practices, tools, and processes. Provide on-call support as required to ensure timely resolution of critical after-hours issues. Perform other duties as assigned. Career Level (P3) Organizational Impact: Works to achieve day-to-day objectives with significant impact on operational results within area of work. Works independently under limited supervision. May be responsible for entire projects or processes within area. Typically, responsible for coaching and reviewing the work of lower-level professionals. Leadership & Talent Management: May be responsible for providing guidance, coaching and training to other employees within functional area. May manage projects at this level, requiring responsibility for the delegation of work and the review of others' work product. Knowledge & Experience: Requires broad knowledge of area typically obtained through advanced education combined with experience. May have practical knowledge of program or project management. Minimum high school diploma or equivalent (GED) required. Typically requires a university degree or equivalent experience and minimum 4-6 years of prior relevant experience. Required Skills Knowledge of DevOps and automation practices, including Azure DevOps, GitHub Actions, Infrastructure as Code (IaC), and Microsoft Power Automate. Experience using monitoring and analytics tools to support automation performance monitoring, operational insights, and issue identification. Experience with scripting, automation, API development, system integration, SDLC, and Agile development methodologies. Strong verbal, written, and interpersonal communication skills with the ability to translate technical concepts for business stakeholders. Ability to balance business objectives with technical solutions to drive process improvement and operational efficiency. Demonstrated analytical thinking, problem-solving capabilities, and the ability to quickly learn and adapt to emerging technologies. Knowledge of information security best practices, including secure credential and secrets management. Strong experience designing, developing, and supporting Robotic Process Automation (RPA) solutions using Microsoft Power Automate, including Cloud Flows, Desktop Flows, and attended/unattended automation. Experience integrating Power Automate with Microsoft 365, SharePoint Online, Teams, Azure services, SQL Server, REST APIs, and other enterprise applications to streamline business processes. Strong understanding of workflow automation, process orchestration, exception handling, automation monitoring, governance, security, and compliance best practices. Experience identifying, analyzing, and transforming manual business, operational, deployment, and support processes into scalable automated workflows that improve efficiency and user experience. Experience implementing automation governance, security, compliance controls, and best practices within enterprise Power Platform environments. Supporting Knowledge Working knowledge of Microsoft Azure, cloud technologies, Infrastructure as Code, Kubernetes, Helm, monitoring tools, operating systems, networking, databases, storage, and Microsoft server technologies to support automation and integration initiatives. Familiarity with AIOps, AI agents, telemetry, AI guardrails, Azure AI Foundry, Copilot Studio, GitHub Copilot, and Power Automate AI capabilities to enhance automation solutions. Experience with the Microsoft Power Platform ecosystem, including Power Apps, Power BI, Dataverse, and Copilot Studio, is preferred. Knowledge of Mortgage Compliance policies is a plus. Physical Requirements: May require travel Pay Range: $123,000.00 - $150,000.00 annually depending on skills and experience In addition to up to 9 paid company holidays per year, employees are eligible for up to 6 days of sick pay. Moreover, eligible employees with less than 10 years of service can accrue up to 17 PTO days per year (and up to 22 PTO days per year upon 10 or more years of service). Employees are eligible to participate in the Company’s 401(k) Plan. Employees (and their eligible dependents) are eligible for medical, dental, and vision insurance coverage. Employees are covered by company-paid disability, basic life insurance and parental leave. Voluntary insurance coverage options, including critical illness, accident, and hospital indemnity, are also available. In addition, the Company offers an Employee Assistance Program and tuition reimbursement (as applicable). Employees may also be eligible for state required benefits such as paid family and medical leave insurance and/or paid sick time as applicable.
